entries.body:
# Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyzes the USDA final rule "Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks" (7 CFR part 2100), published as Federal Register document 2026-13092 on June 29, 2026, and effective July 29, 2026. The rule finalizes the USDA Feedstock Carbon Intensity Calculator (USDA FD-CIC), which quantifies, reports on, and verifies greenhouse gas reduction benefits from low-carbon agricultural practices used to produce biofuel feedstock crops. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The rule "supports the quantification, reporting, and verification of greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction benefits resulting from implementation of low-carbon practices in the production of commodities that are used as biofuel feedstocks in the context of environmental services markets." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* It applies directly to farm producers of covered feedstock crops (field corn, soybeans, sorghum, spring canola) and to the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities handling reduced-carbon-intensity (reduced-CI) crop. For workspaces that arrange transport or forwarding for agricultural biofuel feedstocks, or that serve clients participating in reduced-CI feedstock or sustainable aviation fuel supply chains, this rule sets the federal documentation and carbon-intensity attestation regime those upstream counterparties must meet. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself, as a freight forwarder rather than a farm producer, aggregator, or intermediary entity, falls within any duty-holder class this rule defines.

# Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**MONITORING.** Assess whether any current or prospective client shipping biofuel feedstock crops or reduced-CI processed product relies on USDA FD-CIC certification, since the rule "specifically applies to the production of low- carbon biofuel feedstocks for liquid transportation fuels, which presents a clear environmental services market." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* a forwarder handling reduced-CI feedstock cargo may be asked by shippers to confirm chain-of-custody documentation aligns with the attestation records this rule requires further upstream, even though the forwarder itself is not a named duty-holder in the text. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The rule's obligations attach to farm producers, the first point of aggregation, and intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock supply chain, not to carriers or forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity (e.g., commissioning aggregation, warehousing, or onward distribution of reduced-CI feedstock crop on behalf of a client) brings the workspace within the "first point of aggregation" or "intermediary entities" language the rule uses for its attestation and recordkeeping duties. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Substantive Requirements

**Carbon-intensity quantification and attestation.** Farm producers document field- or management-unit-level carbon intensity using USDA FD-CIC, which "estimates feedstock CIs based on user location, user supplied nutrient management information, and, if applicable, the impact of one or more low-carbon practices." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Recordkeeping and attestation under penalty of perjury.** The Biofuel Feedstock Report submitted by farm producers, and the attestations required of the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities, must be signed under penalty of perjury: the report must "begin with a statement that the undersigned farm producer certifies the following under penalties of perjury." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* this is a federal false-statement liability mechanism, not a stated civil fine amount; a workspace advising a client on documentation integrity for reduced-CI cargo should treat the attestation as carrying personal legal exposure for the signer, distinct from any commercial penalty. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Third-party verification.** Entities "participating in multiple sustainability certification programs must now provide a third-party verifier with documentation related to their participation in those programs... in order to ensure that environmental benefits (i.e., GHG emissions reductions) are not accounted for in multiple programs." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

**Record retention.** Nutrient-management records supporting a claimed low-carbon practice "must be kept for 5 years." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Registration and Reporting Obligations

The rule does not establish a jurisdictional or producer registration scheme; it operates through the Biofuel Feedstock Report and third-party verification process described above rather than a standing agency registration. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-12.*

# Operational System Requirements

For workspaces whose clients are farm producers, aggregators, or intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock chain: (1) confirm the client's Biofuel Feedstock Report and supporting nutrient-management and manure-application records are retained for the 5-year window this rule sets, and (2) confirm any third-party verifier engagement covers all sustainability certification programs the client participates in, to avoid double-counted GHG benefit claims. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.* *Operational implication:* neither requirement creates a direct forwarding-side system build, since the recordkeeping duty sits with the producer, aggregator, or intermediary, not the carrier or forwarder. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- July 29, 2026: rule effective ("DATES: Effective date: July 29, 2026."). In force as of 2026-09-12. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*
- The interim rule preceding this final rule took public comment for 60 days, ending March 18, 2025, and USDA received 114 comments before finalizing the changes reflected in this rule. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.*

# Sources

- Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register document 2026-13092, June 29 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks

metadata.what_is_it: USDA final rule 7 CFR part 2100 Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks Federal Register document 2026-13092 effective July 29 2026 administered by USDA's Office of Energy and Environmental Policy.
metadata.why_matters: The rule governs how USDA FD-CIC carbon-intensity certification and attestation work for reduced-carbon-intensity biofuel feedstock crops. Forwarders handling reduced-CI feedstock or biofuel-adjacent cargo may be asked by shippers to confirm the chain-of-custody documentation this rule requires from upstream farm producers aggregators and intermediary entities is intact. No direct cost or fee attaches to the forwarder under the rule text itself.
key_data: Interim-rule comment period closed March 18 2025 with 114 comments received
Nutrient-management records supporting a low-carbon practice claim must be kept for 5 years
Biofuel Feedstock Report and aggregation/intermediary attestations signed under penalties of perjury
